Primary_Lighting_Directive.Read_First: This directive is read BEFORE every preservation rule below and wins over all of them on the single question of lighting.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Core: This is a RE-RENDER from a single light, NOT a light added on top of the photo. Mental model: treat the photo as a 3D scene; switch OFF all illumination so the scene is momentarily unlit; place exactly ONE new key light directly ABOVE the subject at the vertical zenith (top_90, beam aimed straight down), horizontal direction disabled; then render the whole image using ONLY that one light plus ordinary ambient fill. The original photo's lighting is not dimmed, not blended and not subtracted — it simply never participates in this new render, because the only light sources in the scene now are the new overhead key and ambient fill. Consequence on the SUBJECT'S OWN BODY: the upward-facing planes (top of the head and hair, shoulders, brow ridge, bridge and top of the nose, tops of the cheekbones, upper lip shelf) are directly lit by the new key, while the downward-facing planes (eye sockets, under the brow, under the nose, under the lower lip, under the chin, the neck beneath the jaw, undersides of the arms) are not reached by it and are rendered by ambient fill alone, falling into natural downward shadow. Whatever bright/dark pattern the face had before is gone automatically, not because you erased it, but because the light that drew it is no longer in the scene. If the subject still carries the original front-lit look, you re-rendered on top of the old light instead of replacing it, and the edit has FAILED.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Meaning_Of_Preserve: Every 'preserve / keep / do not change / unchanged' rule below protects SHAPE, GEOMETRY, ANATOMY, COLOR and TEXTURE ONLY. None of them protect the original brightness, the original flat/front lighting, or the original shadow pattern. Re-lighting the subject into an overhead top-lit state is REQUIRED, not optional.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Single_Light_Source_Rule: After this edit the scene contains exactly ONE key light (the new overhead top light) plus ambient fill — nothing else. The original key light has been removed from the scene entirely, so it casts nothing: every highlight and every shadow in the output must be explainable by the new overhead key or by ambient fill alone. This is the whole instruction; there is no list of specific shadows to delete, because you are not deleting anything — you are rendering a scene lit only from directly above, and any plane the overhead key does not reach falls into ambient-filled downward shadow. Test for correctness: pick any shadow or highlight in the result and ask 'which light made this?' If the only honest answer is 'the original front light that is supposed to be gone' (e.g. a front-driven shadow beside the nose surviving on a now top-lit face, a front-driven flat highlight across the whole front of the face), then you have wrongly kept the old light layered under the new one — that is the failure to avoid. Geometry, anatomy, color and texture are unaffected by this rule and stay exactly as in the original; only which light is illuminating them changes.
Primary_Lighting_Directive.Carriers: The new light shows on whichever carriers are present: (1) the SUBJECT'S OWN VOLUME — upward-facing planes lit, downward-facing planes ambient-filled and falling into downward shadow; ALWAYS present, the primary proof of direction, mandatory even for floating or background-less subjects; (2) any real SHADOW-RECEIVING SURFACE — cast shadow falls mostly directly beneath the subject/object; (3) the BACKGROUND — restoring its true luminance so the subject separates is the overhead light acting on it, not a separate effect. Express the direction on every carrier that exists; never leave the subject's own volume unchanged.

Lighting_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, RE-RENDER the image's illumination from a single new overhead key light plus ambient fill, replacing (not adding to) the original lighting, while never changing the content. Apply Primary_Lighting_Directive first, then Original_Image_Preservation_Block, Subject_Preservation_Rule, Universal_Surface_Lighting_Rule, Top_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control, Lighting_Effect_Block, Advanced_Light_Direction_Control, Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule, Light_Intensity_Control, Environment_Lighting_Control, Light_Color_Control, Bright_Background_Compensation_Rule, and Background_Light_Spot_Negative_Rule. When Switch is off, ignore this entire block.

Original_Image_Preservation_Block.Rule: Keep original image structure, aspect ratio, canvas size, framing, camera angle, perspective, crop boundary, subject scale and position, background layout, object placement, geometry, silhouettes, contours, spatial/depth/overlap relationships, color identity, material/skin/hair/fabric/background texture, surface detail, grain, noise and overall composition. The subject, background, props, clothing, accessories, body parts, hair, facial features and contours must not be moved, resized, duplicated, removed, replaced, redrawn, warped, rotated, cropped, reframed, zoomed, reshaped, recolored or recomposed. Only lighting attributes — shadow, highlight, exposure, contrast, illumination direction/intensity, top-plane highlight placement, downward shadow structure, shadow softness/density, cast-shadow behavior and environmental brightness — may be adjusted. Lighting may change perceived brightness and contrast but must not regenerate content.
Original_Image_Preservation_Block.Negative_Rule: No stretching, squeezing, warping, liquify, reshaping, slimming, enlarging, rotating, tilting, added canvas area, face/body reconstruction, pose/hand correction, perspective correction, auto-crop, zoom, reframing, object/background replacement, added/removed objects, style reinterpretation, or retouching beyond lighting-related highlight and shadow changes.

Subject_Preservation_Rule.Applicability: Applies to any identity-bearing living subject (person, character, animal, creature). For products, objects, architecture, interiors, landscapes, vehicles, food or still life, do not force face/eye/anatomy/skin/clothing rules; instead preserve their shape, proportions, material, text, logos, labels, structure, layout, surface detail, seams and edges. For scenes preserve terrain, sky, water, plants, roads, atmosphere, background structure and natural depth. Do not force person-specific lighting onto non-person scenes.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Preserve: Keep the exact original identity and recognizability (same person/animal/character; same age, gender presentation, ethnicity cues, personality, character design); same face shape, proportions and anatomy — brows, eyes, nose, mouth, lips, teeth, jawline, chin, cheekbones, wrinkles, pores, freckles, scars, moles, makeup, facial hair, skin texture and expression; same body shape, proportions, head-to-body ratio, neck, shoulders, torso, limbs, hands, fingers, feet, posture, gesture, pose and silhouette; same hairstyle, length, volume, hairline, direction, texture and color; same clothing design, fit, folds, color, fabric, logos, patterns, accessories, jewelry, glasses, hats, bags, props and object interactions; same subject scale, position, crop boundary, framing, orientation, contact points and subject-to-background relationship. This rule fixes geometry, color and texture only — it does NOT fix brightness, lighting or shadow.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Eye_Gaze: If eyes are present, strictly preserve the original eye gaze, direction, line of sight, pupil and iris position, eyelid shape and openness, eye expression, catchlight position and emotional intent; do not make the subject look at the camera if they were not, or look away if they were, and do not change eye focus, contact, squinting or blinking. Lighting may change highlights and shadows around the eyes only (including deeper eye-socket shadow from the overhead key). If no eyes are present, ignore this and preserve the actual visible content.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Allowed_Changes: Only lighting attributes change: shadow, highlight, exposure, contrast, illumination direction and intensity, top-plane brightness and hardness, downward shadow density and softness, cast-shadow behavior. Per Primary_Lighting_Directive the face, skin and body MUST be visibly re-lit from above; identity, anatomy, texture and color stay the same.
Subject_Preservation_Rule.Negative_Rule: No identity/face/expression/gaze/pose change; no body shape or proportion change; no hairstyle or hair-color change; no clothing or accessory change; no hand/finger/anatomy correction; no beautification, skin smoothing, airbrushing, slimming, aging, de-aging, stylization, realism reinterpretation, character redesign or person replacement; no retouching beyond lighting highlight and shadow changes.

Lighting_Control.Universal_Surface_Lighting_Rule: Apply the selected pure vertical top_90 light to all visible subjects, objects and environment surfaces by their actual geometry. Upward-facing surfaces and top planes receive the light directly; vertical side surfaces receive it only glancingly; undersides, recesses, cavities, overhangs and downward-facing surfaces are turned away from the overhead key and rendered by ambient fill, falling into downward shadow; cast shadows fall mostly directly beneath objects. Product tops, table surfaces, roofs, furniture tops, architecture upper planes, vehicle roofs, foliage canopies, terrain ridges, water surfaces, folds, and head/shoulder tops follow the same top-down direction, falloff and material response. Preserve all original shapes, materials, textures, colors, proportions and spatial relationships. Material response is governed by optical type regardless of direction: opaque solids (stone, metal, wood, plastic, dense fabric) block light into hard-edged top highlights and downward shadow boundaries, with sharp speculars on metal/glossy/wet and diffuse falloff on matte; translucent or thin materials (glass, sheer gauze, thin fabric, leaves, petals, ears, skin and hair edges) transmit and scatter it, glowing with soft subsurface bleed and luminous top-edge transmission. Apply the matching behavior to whatever material is present, preserving original color and texture.

Top_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control.Goal: Make the pure vertical top_90 light reusable across people, products, objects, architecture, interiors, landscapes and full scenes by following upward-facing surfaces, top planes and downward-shadow logic, not only human body parts.
Top_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control.Surface_Rule: The overhead light creates clear top-down modeling: upward-facing surfaces become the brightest, vertical side surfaces read as the planes turned partly away from the light, and undersides or recessed areas fall into downward shadow, making forms read as top-lit. It can model human head/hair/shoulder tops, animal backs, product tops and bevels, furniture tops, roofs and ceiling-facing planes, architectural ledges, vehicles, foliage canopies, terrain ridges, props, folds, cavities and overhangs.
Top_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control.Shadow_Rule: Cast and form shadows fall mostly directly beneath objects and protrusions, consistent with a pure vertical zenith light at the top pole. Avoid diagonal front, side, back or rim-light shadow logic.
Top_Light_Surface_Modeling_Control.Negative_Rule: No front-top reinterpretation, no upper-front light, no beauty light, no side key, no backlight, no rim light, no bottom light, no diagonal cast shadows, no flat frontal fill, no fake spotlight circle, no decorative glow, no object cutout look, no new edges, no altered silhouettes, no recolored materials, no changed geometry.

Lighting_Control.Lighting_Effect_Block: Re-render the image as a scene lit by a SINGLE new key light from directly above the subject/object/scene at the vertical zenith (top_90, beam straight down, horizontal disabled), plus ambient fill — the original illumination is removed from the scene and contributes nothing, so it is replaced, not layered under the new light. Every highlight and shadow in the result must be explainable by the new overhead light or by ambient fill alone; none may trace back to the original front/side key. Preserve subject identity (if people/animals present), facial features, expression, eye gaze, skin/fur texture, body structure, pose, clothing, accessories, props, product shape, text, logos, architecture, furniture, landscape elements, background, composition, original color palette and material/photographic texture. Create clear overhead modeling: upward-facing planes and top surfaces strongly illuminated; downward-facing planes, undersides, eye sockets, under-nose, under-chin, neck and recesses not reached by the overhead key and rendered by ambient fill alone, falling into downward shadow, with no front-driven internal contrast surviving (its old bright/dark pattern is gone because the light that drew it is no longer in the scene); cast shadows falling mostly directly beneath. Photorealistic, pure lighting adjustment only: no fog, haze, extra objects, geometry/subject/face/eye-gaze/pose/clothing change, product or architecture redesign, scene-layout change, recoloring, color cast, background light spots, projected patches, spotlight circles, lens flare, glow blobs, or artificial halos.
Lighting_Control.Bright_Background_Compensation_Rule: If the background is pure white, near-white, overexposed or too bright for the subject/foreground to separate against it, the overhead light acting on the background carrier means reducing only the background luminance/value enough to create clear separation between the visible subject/foreground/scene contour and the background. This is part of re-lighting (the light reaching the background carrier), not a separate effect. Preserve original hue, color identity, saturation relationship, material/photographic texture, background objects, structure and composition. Do not recolor the background, add color cast or colored light, change geometry, add objects, or change the subject/scene. The adjustment must behave like exposure/value reduction only, not color grading, and must support readability without overriding the selected vertical top_90 direction.
Lighting_Control.Background_Light_Spot_Negative_Rule: Do not create any visible light spots, patches, projected circles, spotlight pools, lens flares, glow blobs, artificial halos, bright stains, colored light marks, caustic patterns, bokeh spots, decorative illumination or lamp effects on the background. The background may only receive realistic overall brightness, exposure, contrast and natural downward shadow changes from the selected overhead key direction. Preserve original background texture, color identity, surface material, object structure and composition. Do not add new light shapes or patterns on walls, floor, backdrop, sky, furniture, objects or any background surface.

Advanced_Light_Direction_Control.Rule: Treat the main subject/object/scene center as the center of an imaginary sphere. The light source sits on that sphere and points toward the visible content. For this mode use only the selected pure vertical top_90 direction; the horizontal direction is disabled and must not influence the result. Do not reinterpret as front-top, upper-front, upper-left, upper-right, back-top, side-top, diagonal, front, side, back, bottom or rim. Express the selected top_90 position through highlights on upward-facing planes, downward shadow on undersides and recesses, cast shadows directly beneath, and environmental consistency. Do not alter the original geometry, composition, text, logos or material identity while changing direction.
Advanced_Light_Direction_Control.Ignore_Unselected_Rule: Horizontal_Position_Options and Vertical_Position_Options are a reference menu only. Apply ONLY the option named in Selected_Vertical_Position (top_90); Selected_Horizontal_Position is disabled, so no horizontal option may be applied. All other options are inactive references and must NOT influence the lighting direction, highlights, shadows or cast shadow behavior.
Advanced_Light_Direction_Control.Active_Direction_Prompt: main light source positioned directly above the subject/object/scene at the vertical zenith, pure top_90 overhead light, beam aimed straight down, ceiling-light-like, no horizontal direction, not front, not upper-front, not back, not side, not diagonal, not bottom, not rim. Rays travel vertically downward through the scene. Upward-facing surfaces and top planes get the strongest illumination — head/hair/shoulder tops, animal backs, product tops, furniture tops, table surfaces, vehicle roofs, rooflines, architectural upper planes, foliage canopies, terrain ridges, water surfaces. Downward-facing surfaces, undersides, eye sockets, under-nose, under-chin, neck, cavities and overhangs are turned away from the light and fall into downward shadow; translucent materials (gauze, glass, thin fabric, leaves, hair, skin edges) transmit the light and glow at their top edges. Cast shadows fall mostly directly beneath subjects and objects. Avoid frontal key, upper-front, side, back, bottom-up, rim and colored light. Preserve exact original content, identity and gaze if present, product shape, text, logos, geometry, architecture, scene layout, pose, clothing, body structure and character design.

Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Override_Note: OVERRIDES the lighting implied by every preservation rule above: those rules protect SHAPE, GEOMETRY, COLOR and TEXTURE only, never the original brightness, front/flat lighting or shadow pattern. The subject MUST be re-lit into an overhead top-lit state — upward planes lit, downward planes and recesses in ambient-filled shadow — while identity, anatomy and texture stay unchanged.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Rule: The image is re-rendered as a scene lit by ONE new overhead key light plus ambient fill; the old light is gone from the scene, so the new lighting replaces it rather than being added on top. The change MUST be clearly visible on each carrier present: (1) the SUBJECT'S OWN VOLUME — the upward-facing planes of the head, hair, shoulders, brow, nose bridge, cheekbone tops and every top-facing 3D detail are directly lit by the new key, while the downward-facing planes (eye sockets, under the brow, under the nose, under the lip, under the chin, the neck beneath the jaw, undersides of arms and folds) are not reached by it and are rendered by ambient fill alone, falling into natural downward shadow. Because the original front key is no longer in the scene, no front-driven bright/dark patch may survive — in particular no original nose-side shadow and no flat frontal highlight on the now top-lit face; its old pattern is simply absent, not erased. This carrier is ALWAYS present and mandatory for floating or background-less subjects, where the top-down volume shading alone carries the effect. (2) any real SHADOW-RECEIVING SURFACE (ground, floor, table, nearby objects) — cast shadow falls mostly directly beneath the subject/object. (3) the BACKGROUND — when too bright for separation, its true luminance is restored. Do not artificially darken or brighten either the top or the underside — render the real physical result and let translucent materials glow. The result must look clearly top-lit and different from the original in light and shadow, while remaining the exact same subject, geometry, color, texture and composition.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Surface_Absence_Rule: If a shadow-receiving surface is genuinely absent or too far to catch a realistic cast shadow (subject against open sky, a seamless backdrop or a gradient), do not fabricate fake ground or background shadows; in that case carrier (1) — the top-lit upward planes plus ambient-filled downward shadow on the subject's own volume — alone must carry the full overhead effect. When a valid surface IS present, the cast shadow beneath and the subject modeling must show the change together.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Negative_Rule: Do not output flat, even, frontal, ambient or original-style uniform lighting on the subject; do not let the key light still reach the front of the face as if from the camera direction; do not let the subject look unchanged from the original; do not treat 'preserve identity/skin/face' as a reason to skip re-lighting; do not issue brightness-operation instructions such as 'darken / dim / brighten / lift / crush the undersides' — describe only the physics (key from directly above, undersides ambient-filled) and let the shading be the natural result; do not render top highlights as a flat graphic stroke, sticker outline, neon border or detached halo; do not add fake background shadows on sky or seamless backdrops; do not express the overhead light on only one carrier while leaving the subject's own volume unchanged.
Dual_Carrier_Lighting_Rule.Horizontal_Position_Options_Note: DISABLED in top_90 mode. The horizontal menu (front, front_right, right, back_right, back, back_left, left, front_left) is an inactive reference only and must NOT influence direction, highlights, shadows or cast shadows; the light stays at the pure vertical zenith.

Vertical_Position_Options.top_90: light source directly above the subject at +90 degrees elevation, pure zenith, beam aimed vertically downward. Strongest highlights on upward-facing surfaces, top planes and upper edges; side surfaces darker; undersides, recesses and lower planes fall into deep shadow. Cast shadows fall mostly directly beneath. Ignore horizontal direction.
Vertical_Position_Options.upper_45: light source above the subject at about +45 degrees elevation, between horizontal and top, beam aimed diagonally downward. Upper planes and surfaces facing the selected horizontal position receive highlights; lower planes, undersides and opposite-facing surfaces fall into controlled shadow. Cast shadows travel diagonally downward and away.
Vertical_Position_Options.horizontal_0: light source positioned at 0 degrees elevation on the horizontal plane around the subject, at approximately mid-height. The rays travel horizontally, parallel to the ground, striking the subject from the selected horizontal position at the same vertical height, not from above or below. Surfaces facing the light are illuminated, opposite-facing surfaces fall into shadow, while top- and bottom-facing planes receive little direct light. Cast shadows extend mainly horizontally away from the selected direction. Avoid overhead and bottom-up lighting.
Vertical_Position_Options.lower_45: light source positioned below the subject at about -45 degrees elevation, halfway between the horizontal plane and the bottom pole. The rays travel diagonally upward toward the subject, not vertically. Lower-facing surfaces, undersides, bottom edges and surfaces facing the selected horizontal position receive stronger illumination; upper and top-facing surfaces become relatively darker but stay partially readable. Cast shadows move diagonally upward and away, following the selected horizontal position and the low angle. A low-position diagonal key light, not a pure bottom light.
Vertical_Position_Options.bottom_minus_90: light source positioned directly below the subject at -90 degrees elevation, pure nadir bottom position, beam aimed vertically upward. An extreme direct bottom light, not a diagonal low-angle light. Strongest highlights appear almost exclusively on undersides, bottom planes, lower edges and downward-facing surfaces; front, side and top-facing surfaces receive little direct light and top planes fall into deep upward shadow. Shadows project vertically upward from protrusions, cavities and overhangs. The result feels unnatural, severe and unmistakably bottom-lit. Ignore horizontal direction.

Light_Intensity_Control.Rule: Use only the selected intensity level. The Intensity_Value controls strength, contrast, shadow density, highlight brightness, shadow edge sharpness and falloff of the selected overhead key light. Do not change the subject, eye gaze, direction or expression while adjusting intensity.
Light_Intensity_Control.Active_Intensity_Prompt: medium-intensity true vertical top light, controlled overhead highlights on upward-facing surfaces and top planes, clear downward shadow structure under brow, nose, chin and recesses, moderate contrast, moderate shadow density, ambient-filled undersides with detail intact, realistic falloff across people, animals, products, objects, architecture, interiors and landscapes, no extreme overexposure, preserve original color, identity, product shape, text, logos, pose, clothing, geometry and material texture

Intensity_Levels.20: soft low-intensity key light, gentle illumination, low contrast, light shadows, soft shadow edges, subtle highlights, weak sculptural form, natural low-power lighting
Intensity_Levels.40: moderate-low intensity key light, controlled illumination, mild contrast, visible but not harsh shadows, moderate shadow softness, restrained highlights, gentle facial sculpting
Intensity_Levels.60: medium-intensity cinematic key light, balanced contrast, clear highlight and shadow structure, defined facial volume, moderate shadow density, realistic falloff, controlled dramatic lighting
Intensity_Levels.80: strong high-intensity key light, high contrast, sharp shadow structure, dense shadows, bright highlights, strong sculptural form, dramatic directional lighting, clear falloff
Intensity_Levels.90: very strong high-intensity key light, very bright highlights, high contrast, hard highlights, dense opposite-side shadows, strong separation, clear falloff
Intensity_Levels.100: extreme high-intensity hard key light, very high contrast, very sharp shadow edges, deep black shadows, intense specular highlights, harsh falloff, powerful sculptural lighting, severe dramatic illumination

Environment_Lighting_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, apply the selected lighting direction and intensity to the subject, objects and surrounding environment/background by physical surface orientation and scene geometry. The environment may receive general brightness, exposure, contrast change, natural downward cast-shadow direction beneath objects, top-plane illumination consistency and subtle brightness consistency, but must not generate visible light spots, projected circles, decorative patches, glow blobs, halos, lens flares or artificial bright stains. When Switch is off, apply the lighting mainly to the main visible content while preserving the original background. Do not change background objects, subject identity, object/product shape, text, logos, architecture, position, composition, eye gaze or scene layout. Environmental lighting must support the selected vertical top_90 direction, not flatten it.
Environment_Lighting_Control.Environment_Prompt: extend the vertical overhead top light into the surrounding environment only through realistic overall illumination, top-plane brightness consistency, natural downward cast-shadow direction beneath objects, general exposure shift and subtle brightness consistency. Make visible content and environment share the same top_90 overhead direction and medium intensity. Upward-facing surfaces (product tops, table surfaces, furniture tops, vehicle roofs, rooflines, architecture upper planes, foliage canopies, terrain ridges) may gain top highlights; vertical side surfaces read darker, undersides and recesses fall into downward shadow, and cast shadows fall mostly directly beneath. Preserve original color palette, material colors, photographic texture, atmosphere, background objects, subject identity, face and gaze if present, body/clothing/pose, product shape, text, logos, geometry, architecture, landscape structure and composition. No light spots, projected circles, spotlight pools, lens flare, glow blobs, artificial halos, decorative patterns or lamp effects on walls, floor, backdrop, sky, furniture or background; no colored spill or tint; no object/subject/product/architecture/scene-layout change; no gaze change if eyes present; no front, side, back, bottom or rim light.

Light_Color_Control.Rule: When Switch is on, apply Main_Light_Color to the selected directional key light. When off, ignore this entire Light_Color_Control block and keep the light color natural or unchanged.
Light_Color_Control.Effect_Block: ignored because Light_Color_Control is off; no color gel lighting, no artificial colored light, no warm yellow overlay, no red tint, no blue tint, preserve natural or original light color
